findings.claim: The managed span shipped to every consumer states: "`totem init` installs `/signon`, `/signoff`, `/review-reply` and `/review-loop`" — and the changeset (line 5) lists "the installed skills" as part of "the product-valid instruction set any consumer gets."
findings.counterexample: OBSERVED. The four skills are written only inside `for (const tool of selectedTools) { if (!tool.hookInstaller) continue; ... }` (init.ts:1831-1833 → `installClaudeHooks`, init.ts:512, skills loop at init.ts:583-586), i.e. only when Claude Code is BOTH detected and selected, and only into `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`. The floor scaffold runs unconditionally at init.ts:1675, BEFORE `if (options?.bare)` at init.ts:1688 — so `totem init --bare` (which logs 'Skipping AI tool and hook installation for bare mode.') writes an AGENTS.md asserting an install that bare mode never performs. Directly visible in the existing suite's own output: `pnpm exec vitest run src/commands/init.test.ts` → 'initCommand non-interactive mode > runs to completion with --yes on a TTY' prints `OK AGENTS.md — Scaffolded the AGENTS.md floor` with NO `.claude/skills/...` row in the same summary. A Gemini-CLI-only or Cursor-only consumer gets the same false sentence, and the `.agents/skills/` twin is a hand copy until mmnto-ai/totem#2788 (AGENTS.md:65, overlay §1 line 12). The sterility test cannot catch this class — it checks lexicon, never product truth.

findings.claim: `scrubAgentsFloor`'s doc: "the repository's own content on either side is kept" / changeset line 5: "`totem eject` removes the span ... keeping the repository's content around it byte-exact." Its docstring adds "An unpaired or inverted marker is never attributed and never scrubbed."
findings.counterexample:
OBSERVED. Pairing is `content.indexOf(AGENTS_FLOOR_START)` (717) + `content.indexOf(AGENTS_FLOOR_END)` (718) — first-start/first-end. Ran `scrubAgentsFloor` against `# Mine
<START>
MY OWN TEXT
<START>
x
<END>

## Keep
`: result `"# Mine

## Keep
"`, summary `{"scrubbed":["AGENTS.md"]}` — the user's line `MY OWN TEXT` was deleted and reported as a clean scrub. The function this one cites as its model deliberately does the opposite: `scrubReflexFiles` pairs END-anchored, `const startIdx = out.lastIndexOf(REFLEX_START, endIdx)` (eject.ts:845), whose comment names this exact hazard — "an orphan START from that same pre-fix damage sitting ABOVE a complete block never widens the removal span" (mmnto-ai/totem#2602). A duplicated start marker is a normal git-merge-conflict residue in a markdown file.

OBSERVED. `scrubAgentsFloor` removes exactly one span (no loop). Input `# Mine

<BLOCK>

MID

<BLOCK>

## Keep
` → output retains the SECOND complete managed block verbatim (start marker through end marker, all 1,932 bytes) while the summary reports `scrubbed: ["AGENTS.md"]`. The cited precedent loops — `for (;;) { const endIdx = out.indexOf(REFLEX_END, searchStart); ... }` (eject.ts:843ff), whose comment states the contract as "loops until no complete pair remains". Post-eject, `totem doctor`/a later `totem init` still sees a live managed span in a repo the user was told was ejected.

findings.claim: "`totem eject` removes the span (and the file, when the span was all it held), keeping the repository's content around it byte-exact."
findings.counterexample:
OBSERVED, two ways. (a) CRLF: scrubbing a CRLF file `# Mine

intro

<BLOCK>

## Rules
` yields `"# Mine

intro

## Rules
"` — the user's own line `intro
` came back as `intro
`, a byte of repository content changed and a bare LF injected into an otherwise-CRLF file. Cause: `before = content.slice(0, startIdx).replace(/(?:?
)*$/, '
')` (eject.ts:745) hardcodes LF. (b) LF: the same line collapses any number of blank lines above the span to one, so a deliberate two-blank-line gap is not preserved. The code comment is honest ("the seam normalized ... one blank line where the span sat"); the changeset's "byte-exact" is not. Same seam shape as `scrubReflexFiles` (eject.ts:863), so the code matches precedent — the changeset sentence is the defect.

findings.claim: "Every later `totem init` refreshes exactly the span and leaves every other byte alone." (changeset line 5 repeats it: "refreshes exactly the bytes from the start marker through the end marker and leaves every other byte alone".)
findings.counterexample:
OBSERVED. `scaffoldAgentsFloor` pairs `existing.indexOf(AGENTS_FLOOR_START)` (init.ts:761) with `existing.indexOf(AGENTS_FLOOR_END)` (init.ts:762). Ran it on `# Mine
<START>
MY OWN TEXT
<START>
x
<END>
` → `{action:'refreshed'}` and the output begins `# Mine
<START>
<!-- Managed by ...` — `MY OWN TEXT` and the second start marker are gone. So the refresh CAN write outside the intended span and silently eat repository content. (This one matches init.ts's own precedent — `upgradeReflexes` uses the same first-index pairing at init.ts:1131-1132 — so it is the doc claim that is false, and the fix that eject already has, F2, is the one init lacks.) Verified separately: on the ordinary paths the claim holds — a second scaffold on its own output is `unchanged` with byte-identical content, and the documented adoption path (user adds the two bare marker lines, re-runs) produces `refreshed` then `unchanged` with surrounding bytes intact.

findings.claim: Shipped template sentence: "Private or team-only instructions, when present, resolve from an installed doctrine package and are never committed here."
findings.counterexample: OBSERVED. No shipped code resolves instructions from a doctrine package. The product's only doctrine-package wiring is `totem init --doctrine`, hardcoded to the private cohort package — `export const DOCTRINE_PIN_PACKAGE = '@mmnto/strategy-doctrine'` (init-doctrine.ts:26) pointing `orient.parityManifest` at `node_modules/@mmnto/strategy-doctrine/parity-manifest.yaml` (init-doctrine.ts:34), a parity manifest, not instructions. `grep -rn "cohort-overlay" packages/*/src/ --include=*.ts` (non-test) returns only prose comments in wt.ts and estate-scan.ts — nothing reads `cohort-overlay.md`. A consumer cannot act on this sentence; it describes a cohort arrangement in product voice.

findings.claim: The test header claims it catches "a private repository path, a deployment name, an operator fingerprint, a doctrine tag a public reader cannot follow, an unqualified issue reference, or a relative link that does not resolve".
findings.counterexample: OBSERVED by evaluating the exact lexicons against mutants. Caught: `mmnto-ai/totem-strategy:doctrine/x.md`, `#123`, `(#456)`, `strategy#622`, `totem#2801`, `Tenet 20`, `ADR-105`, `Proposal 213`/`Prop 305`, `totem-claude`/`strategy-claude`/`status-claude`/`lc-claude`, `cohort`/`falsification`. NOT caught: `adr-105`, `ADR 105`, `tenet 20`, `Tenet-16`, `proposal 213` (all four DENY_PATTERNS are case-sensitive and hyphen/space-rigid, lines 74-79); `the totem-strategy repo has doctrine` (DENY_SUBSTRINGS has `mmnto-ai/totem-strategy` and `totem-strategy:` but not the bare repo name, line 63-64); `the agy seat ruled it` (AGENT_ID line 82 requires a `<repo>-<vendor>` shape); `the operator runs Windows 11` and `solo-operator repo` — the "operator fingerprint" class is three substrings only (`satur8d`, `skynet`, `arhgap`, lines 68-70) while overlay §3 line 29 names the operator environment as "solo-operator + bot-review repo; Windows 11 host". Confirmed no false positives: `Properties 3` / `Propose 3` do not match `/\bProp(?:osal)?\.? ?\d+/`, and `mmnto-ai/totem#123` is correctly exempt from BARE_REF while `Closes #NNN` is correctly ignored (non-digit). Enumeration is a legitimate design; the docstring states it as class coverage.

findings.claim: Changeset line 7: "it probes every URL, qualified issue ref and qualified path a file carries without a token and reports the ones a public reader cannot follow."
findings.counterexample: OBSERVED from the regex set (lines 37-40). Missed shapes a public reader also cannot follow: a bare repo reference `mmnto-ai/totem-strategy` with no `#N` and no `:path` (no regex covers it — this shape is live today at `.gemini/styleguide.md:137`); `owner/repo@sha` (the shape that existed at origin/main in `.claude/docs/contributing.md`, `mmnto-ai/totem-playground@80b4d1b`, and which this diff removed by hand, not by the script); reference-style links `[x]: path`; pure-anchor links `[x](#a)` (MD_LINK_RE's `([^)\s#]+)` requires ≥1 non-`#` char); qualified paths with no file extension (`owner/repo:adr/**`). Verified clean on the credential question: the code reads no env var, builds only `user-agent`, and Node's global fetch (undici) reads neither `GH_TOKEN` nor `HTTP_PROXY` by default — OBSERVED in source, no leak path. 3xx handling is correct: `redirect: 'follow'` means `response.status` is the terminal status and `ok = status < 400`. Live run over the seven public surfaces: 8 references, 8 resolve, exit 0.

findings.claim: "%s: every relative link resolves to a file in the tree" — `expect(fs.existsSync(path.resolve(dir, target))).toBe(true)`.
findings.counterexample: INFERRED from platform semantics: NTFS is case-insensitive, so `[Architecture](.claude/Docs/architecture.md)` passes `existsSync` on this win32 host and 404s on github.com, which is case-sensitive. The assertion is weaker than the class-5 clause it implements ("Every ref in the committed file resolves unauthenticated", 619 comment 10 line 49) on exactly the platform the operator authors on.

findings.claim: Row 13 ruled the T0 stanza verbatim: "The floor keeps what a contributor needs and can verify publicly: this repo uses bot reviewers; review triggers are the maintainer's to post, never an agent's; ..."
findings.counterexample: OBSERVED. The committed floor says "If this repository uses review bots: review triggers are the maintainer's to post..." — a conditional where the ruling wrote a statement of fact about this repository. All five ruled elements are present (triggers/maintainer, `/review-reply`, one dispositions comment per round, never cite an unpushed commit, zero private refs, zero section numbers), so the row is substantially applied; the hedge is a consequence of the floor and the generic template being the same bytes, and it means totem's own AGENTS.md no longer asserts that totem uses bot reviewers.

findings.claim: Row 4 ruled Session Start items 1, 2, 3, 5 **FLOOR** — "Product-valid for any consumer", i.e. kept, not reworded away.
findings.counterexample: OBSERVED. Old item 5 was "Don't push speculative fixes. Run `totem lint` locally — front-load all checks before the first push" (origin/main AGENTS.md:17). New item 4 is "Run `totem lint` locally before the first push; front-load the deterministic checks." The imperative "Don't push speculative fixes" is dropped, and "all checks" narrowed to "the deterministic checks". Both edits are defensible T0 prose, but row 4 carried no REWORD disposition — it is the one FLOOR row whose content changed.

findings.claim: Row 21 ruled the agent-bus prose **DELETE** — "Overlay § 4 carries the whole contract; nothing here is floor content"; the operator block authorized keeping only "the marker as the single declared exception in the repo block".

The deleted prose is gone (verified: no 'Lane table', no mmnto-ai/totem-strategy#697/#639, no judgment-density classes, no parity-row sentence), and the marker is preserved byte-exact at AGENTS.md:69 — `totem doctor --parity` OBSERVED green: `PASS — agent-bus declared — role "bus" → seat "totem-claude" in AGENTS.md`, and the marker sits at line 69, OUTSIDE the managed span (end marker at line 36), so an init refresh cannot wipe the sensor. findings.claim: The dispatch (2026-09-12T17:43Z) asked the cold-start line be worded "after the seat-and-assignment step" in the floor; row 22 keeps the cold-start line FLOOR.

findings.claim: `renderAgentsFloorScaffold` instructs the consumer: "keep tool-specific instruction files as thin redirects to it."
findings.counterexample: OBSERVED. The same `totem init` run injects `AI_PROMPT_BLOCK` — 8,564 bytes, measured — into every tool reflex file: `CLAUDE.md`, `GEMINI.md`, `.cursorrules`, `.junie/guidelines.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md` (init-detect.ts:99-123). The scaffold tells the consumer to keep those thin while the tool makes them 8.5 KB. Note the product's own redirect gate sets the threshold at 600 bytes (`CLAUDE_MD_REDIRECT_MAX_BYTES`, doctor.ts:1197).

findings.claim: [NOTE] `deriveProjectName` — "the package name with any npm scope stripped, else the directory basename ... a title string, never load-bearing".
findings.counterexample: OBSERVED, answering the charge's question (e): it never throws, but it CAN return an empty string — `{"name":"@acme/"}` → `""` (the `replace(/^@[^/]+\//, '')` consumes the whole trimmed name), and `deriveProjectName('C:\\')` → `""` (path.basename of a drive root), both yielding a title `# : Agent Instructions`. It also does not sanitize: `{"name":"evil\n# Injected Heading"}` renders verbatim into the scaffold's H1, minting a second heading. The three `deriveProjectName` tests (init.test.ts:4251-4274) cover scoped / unscoped / missing-or-unparseable and none of these; the sterility test renders only `'example'` and `'widgets'`. Low impact (a local package.json the user owns), disclosed as a coverage shape.

findings.claim: [NOTE] "`unchanged` — markers present, span already canonical (byte no-op)" / the charge's question (a): is a second scaffold on its own output a byte no-op in every case, including CRLF?
findings.counterexample: OBSERVED. On its own output, always yes. On a CRLF working tree (autocrlf checkout of a committed LF span) the FIRST call returns `refreshed` and rewrites the span to LF, leaving a file with CRLF outside the span and LF inside; the second call returns `unchanged` and content is stable. So: converges after one write, no flip-flop, no corruption — but a consumer on a CRLF checkout sees a "Refreshed the managed AGENTS.md span" row on the first init after every fresh clone, and gets mixed line endings. Not an issue for this repo: `.gitattributes` is `* text=auto eol=lf`, and `AGENTS.md` on disk has 0 CR bytes, so the byte-identity assertion at agents-floor-sterility.test.ts:113 is safe here.

findings.claim: [NOTE] `it('keeps the search_knowledge instruction inside the managed span')`.
findings.counterexample: OBSERVED. The body is `expect(AGENTS_FLOOR_BLOCK).toContain('search_knowledge')` — a substring check on the constant, not on the committed file and not on the instruction. It would pass on any stray mention and is wholly subsumed by the byte-identity assertion five lines above (line 113). Zero added strength; harmless.

verdict: The ruling is applied faithfully in substance: I walked all 24 rows of mmnto-ai/totem-strategy#619 comment 10 against the new AGENTS.md, and every DELETE row is carried by the pinned overlay — row 5 and row 24 by cohort-overlay.md §1 bullet 1, row 10 verbatim by §2, row 14 by §1's cr-disclaimer bullet, row 15 by §1's cite map plus §2's memory-pointer bullet, row 21 wholly by §4 (items 2/3/5 plus succession), row 3 by §1's new delta-A bullet and row 9's T1 half by delta B's trailing clause in §1 — so there is no BLOCKING finding: no deleted line is homeless and no byte-corruption path exists on the ordinary scaffold/refresh/eject routes (idempotency, marker-adoption, preserved-file and file-removal paths all verified empirically against the built dist). Row 11's acceptance item is genuinely cured (AI_PROMPT_BLOCK is defined at init-templates.ts:18 and only imported by init.ts), /signon is added per row 16, row 2 uses the ruled A1 line with zero em-dashes in the file, both of strategy-claude's dispatch reads are carried, the class-5 network test passes 8/8 with zero unresolvable refs, mmnto-ai/totem#2866 and #2788 are real and public, and the three named regression gates are green (agents-floor-sterility 28/28, config-drift 58/58 with both crossVendorCanonical and .junie/guidelines.md satisfied, init+eject 382 passed, doctor --claim-discipline PASS non-vacuously over 485 compiled rules, doctor --parity agent-bus PASS). What survives falsification are five MATERIAL items the seat should rule before merge: one false product claim now being written into every consumer's repository (F1 — the template asserts an install that bare mode, and any non-Claude consumer, never performs), two marker-pairing defects in scrubAgentsFloor that delete user content and leave a live span behind a "scrubbed" report (F2, F3) where the function's own cited precedent scrubReflexFiles already solved both under mmnto-ai/totem#2602, the same first-index pairing on the init side contradicting the wiki's "leaves every other byte alone" (F5), and the changeset's "byte-exact" seam claim which CRLF falsifies outright (F4). The sterility sensor does what it says within an enumerated lexicon but is case-sensitive and misses the bare private-repo name and most operator-environment fingerprints (F7); the resolvability script is honest about credentials and redirects but not about "every" reference shape (F8). [Seat's fold, appended: all seventeen folded in the commit that follows cc8c9918 — END-anchored pairing shared by init and eject with a loop in eject and a second-span hint in init (F2, F3, F5), EOL-aware spans and seams (F4, F16), the three template sentences corrected and the doctrine line moved to this repository's declared block (F1, F6, F13, F14), the floor's row-4 wording restored and the review-bots fact and the agent-bus sentence restated (F10, F11, F12), the sterility lexicon made case- and separator-insensitive with the bare repository name and the operator token added, the relative-link check made case-exact, the redundant test removed and the docstring narrowed to an enumerated lexicon (F7, F9, F17), the script's commit-ref and reference-style-link shapes added and its non-extracted shapes named in the header with the changeset claim narrowed to match (F8), the project name never empty and never multi-line (F15).]
